title: Substitute into the Definition
text:
With $f(x) = \frac{1}{x}$, we have:

$f(x+h) = \frac{1}{x+h}$

So the difference quotient is:

$$\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{\frac{1}{x+h} - \frac{1}{x}}{h}$$

title: Find Common Denominator
text:
Simplify the numerator by finding a common denominator:

$$\frac{1}{x+h} - \frac{1}{x} = \frac{x - (x+h)}{x(x+h)} = \frac{-h}{x(x+h)}$$

So the difference quotient becomes:

$$\frac{\frac{-h}{x(x+h)}}{h}$$

title: The Simplified Quotient
text:
The difference quotient simplifies to:

$$\frac{-h}{x(x+h) \cdot h} = \frac{-h}{hx(x+h)}$$

Now we can cancel the $h$ (for $h \neq 0$).
